nodes.summary: Arithmetic circuits over a field and the complexity of algebraic problems: matrix multiplication exponents (square, rectangular, dual) and their bounds, tensor rank, and the bit complexity of integer multiplication.
nodes.title: Algebraic complexity

nodes.summary: Boolean circuits as a model of computation, including arithmetic circuits built from gates (adders, two's complement), parallel classes AC0, NC1 and NC, and circuit lower bounds (parity and majority not in AC0, Smolensky, Razborov's monotone bound, Shannon counting, Williams).
nodes.title: Boolean circuit complexity

nodes.summary: Problems complete for classes other than NP: P (circuit value), NL (s-t connectivity), coNP (UNSAT), PSPACE (TQBF, Geography), levels of the polynomial hierarchy (QSAT_k), EXP, NEXP and EXPSPACE (succinct problems, regular expressions with squaring).
nodes.title: Completeness for other complexity classes

nodes.summary: Definitions of time and space complexity on machine models (P, NP, PSPACE, EXP, L, NL, the polynomial hierarchy, FPT and W[1]), polynomial-time encodings and reductions, simulation overheads, Blum measures, and inclusions and collapses among deterministic and nondeterministic classes (Savitch, Immerman–Szelepcsényi, Karp–Lipton, Ladner, Mahaney). Randomized, counting, circuit and quantum classes have their own…
nodes.title: Complexity classes

nodes.summary: Recursive and recursively enumerable predicates and their closure properties, the halting problem, Rice's and Rice–Shapiro theorems, the recursion and s-m-n theorems, enumerators, index sets such as totality, finiteness and minimal programs, and Busy Beaver functions.
nodes.title: Computability and undecidability

nodes.summary: Context-free grammars and derivations, normal forms, parsing algorithms, pushdown automata, deterministic and ambiguous languages, closure and non-closure properties, pumping and Ogden's lemmas, and Parikh images.
nodes.title: Context-free languages

nodes.summary: Context-sensitive grammars, linear bounded automata and space-bounded single-tape machines, and the equivalence between them.
nodes.title: Context-sensitive languages

nodes.summary: \#P and PP: #P-completeness (counting SAT, permanent), PP-completeness, Toda's theorem, threshold languages, and approximate counting algorithms and schemes (Stockmeyer, Karp–Luby, Jerrum–Sinclair–Vigoda).
nodes.title: Counting complexity

nodes.summary: Algorithms deciding questions about finite automata, regular expressions and context-free grammars given as data: emptiness, membership, universality, equivalence, and computable grammar reduction, together with the encodings of automata and grammars they operate on; and satisfiability of string constraints (word equations with regular membership and length bounds).
nodes.title: Decision procedures for automata, grammars and strings

nodes.summary: Turing and many-one reducibility, Turing degrees and the jump, recursive isomorphism (Myhill), productive, creative, simple and immune sets, r.e.-completeness, and the arithmetical hierarchy.
nodes.title: Degrees of unsolvability and the arithmetical hierarchy

nodes.summary: Logical characterizations of complexity classes on finite structures: Fagin's theorem, Immerman–Vardi (least fixed point and P), and transitive closure logic and NL.
nodes.title: Descriptive complexity

nodes.summary: Register (URM), counter and RAM machines, and theorems that Turing machines and other models compute exactly the partial recursive functions or decide and recognize exactly the recursive and r.e. predicates (Church–Turing equivalences).
nodes.title: Equivalence of models of computation

nodes.summary: Exact running times of hard problems beyond the polynomial/non-polynomial divide: exponential, subexponential and quasipolynomial algorithms for NP-hard or NP-intermediate problems, such as the tensor-network 2^o(n)-time algorithm for 3-SAT and Babai's quasipolynomial-time graph isomorphism theorem, and the exponential time hypothesis.
nodes.title: Fine-grained and exponential-time complexity

nodes.summary: Time and space hierarchy theorems and diagonalization against time-bounded machines, separations such as P ≠ EXP, and barriers to separating classes: relativization (Baker–Gill–Solovay, oracle separations), natural proofs and algebrization.
nodes.title: Hierarchy theorems and proof barriers

nodes.summary: Algorithmic information content of individual strings: universal description methods, incompressible strings, non-computability and upper semicomputability of Kolmogorov complexity.
nodes.title: Kolmogorov complexity

nodes.summary: The Cook–Levin theorem and NP-completeness of specific decision problems, by the problem's domain; includes both machine-level Karp reductions and stated NP-completeness results.
nodes.title: NP-completeness

nodes.summary: Büchi, generalized Büchi, parity, Rabin, Streett and Muller automata on infinite words, their emptiness and conversions, and parity games with attractors and traps.
nodes.title: Automata on infinite words and infinite games

nodes.summary: The PCP theorem and Dinur's gap amplification, optimization classes (NPO, APX, MAXSNP), and hardness of approximation results such as Håstad's MAX-3SAT bound and the absence of a PTAS for MAX-CUT.
nodes.title: Probabilistically checkable proofs and inapproximability

nodes.summary: Proofs or statements that specific problems lie in P or L: graph reachability (PATH) with its marking machine, undirected connectivity in L, 2-SAT, primality, matching, maximum flow, linear programming, integer programming in fixed dimension, and hypergraph matching and cut questions.
nodes.title: Problems solvable in polynomial time

nodes.summary: Complexity-theoretic foundations of cryptography and derandomization: one-way functions, hardcore predicates (Goldreich–Levin), hardness amplification (Yao's XOR lemma), hardness-versus-randomness generators (Nisan–Wigderson), and Impagliazzo's five worlds.
nodes.title: Pseudorandomness and one-way functions

nodes.summary: Probabilistic classes (RP, BPP), Arthur–Merlin and interactive proofs (AM, MA, IP = PSPACE, graph (non)isomorphism), BPP versus nonuniform and alternating classes, randomized reductions (Valiant–Vazirani), and quantum classes BQP and QMA.
nodes.title: Randomized, interactive and quantum complexity

nodes.summary: Deterministic, nondeterministic, two-way and ε-automata, transducers, regular expressions and Kleene's theorem, closure properties of regular languages, automaton minimization, and the algebraic theory of recognition by monoids.
nodes.title: Finite automata and regular languages

nodes.summary: Definitions, semantics and programming of Turing machines (single-tape, multi-tape and multi-stack), simulations between tape models, and universal machines with their machine codes. Results showing that a model computes exactly the recursive functions go to Equivalence of models of computation.
nodes.title: Turing machines

nodes.summary: Specific undecidable problems and the reductions proving them undecidable: the Post correspondence problem and its variants, string rewriting, undecidable questions about context-free grammars (ambiguity, intersection, universality, regularity), and emptiness of linear bounded automata.
nodes.title: Undecidable problems

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
